title: The WLM Local Group dwarf galaxy

story: This image shows WLM, a dwarf galaxy in the Local Group, the family of galaxies that includes our Milky Way. It lies in the constellation Cetus.

Dwarf galaxies are small galaxies containing far fewer stars than large spirals such as the Milky Way. Because they are small and faint, the nearby ones in the Local Group are particularly valuable, since their individual stars can be studied in detail.

The picture was taken with the Mosaic II camera on the CTIO Blanco 4-m telescope as part of the Local Group Survey, a project sponsored by NOAO and led by Philip Massey of Lowell Observatory. The survey imaged galaxies through a set of broadband filters and also through filters tuned to specific glowing gases, and it made all of its data and measurements available through a public website.

understand.summary: This is a true-color combination of images taken through three of the survey's filters with the Mosaic II camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope. The source does not say which three filters were used.
